project: rauf — ux-overhaul-grammar (Phase 2+3: command grammar & contract flip, v0.5.0)
description: Phase 2+3 of the rauf UX/DX overhaul as one breaking v0.5.0 flip: collapse loop run/loop start into `loop run --detached`, normalize the flag canon, unify exit codes across status + loop run, add an explicit `review` signal, and formalize events.ndjson versioning. Surface + contract change — the execution engine, server daemon, and Phase-1 observation substrate are reused. Specs in specs/ux-overhaul-grammar/ (00-06 + TRACEABILITY); cross-cutting canon in specs/ux-overhaul/CANON.md. feature-forge lockstep edits + the v0.5.0 tag/release are an OUT-OF-LOOP manual cutover step (REQ-CONTRACT-04/05) — intentionally NOT in this backlog. Dogfood with the frozen rauf-stable binary; the version bump (013) does not affect the running loop.

Do NOT change `LoopStateSignalSchema` (~line 183 = clean|blocked|needs_human|error) — that is state.json.lastSignal, a separate vocabulary. Do not touch the runner yet (the collapse removal is item 002). This item only widens the schema enum.

items.title: Redefine ExitCode to the unified table + re-point all CLI call sites (atomic)
items.description: Redefine the `ExitCode` const in packages/cli/src/commands.ts (~lines 90-101) to the unified canon table from 00-core-definitions.md §1: SUCCESS=0, ERROR=1, USAGE=2, NEEDS_HUMAN=3, LIMIT=4, BLOCKED=5, RUNNING=6. Then re-point EVERY call site across the CLI package per the 03-exit-codes.md §2 remap: INVALID_ARGS→USAGE (rename, same value 2); NOT_FOUND→USAGE(2); VALIDATION→USAGE(2); CONFLICT→USAGE(2) (incl. loop-already-running 409); PAUSED_HUMAN→NEEDS_HUMAN(3). This is a HARD COMPILE BREAK that MUST land as ONE atomic commit — the build is never red mid-sweep. Affected files (per 03 §2): commands.ts (the const + its own uses incl. dispatch fallback), backlog-commands.ts, install-commands.ts, profile-config-commands.ts, migrate-commands.ts, reset-commands.ts, resume-commands.ts, main.ts, follow-command.ts, server-commands.ts (~:406/:630 CONFLICT→USAGE), loop-commands.ts (the 4 CONFLICT→USAGE loop-already-running/lock-conflict sites ~:305/:672/:691/:711 — NOT :982, which is item 004's loop-run terminal mapping). Update commands.test.ts AND loop-commands.test.ts (~:597/:733/:760 CONFLICT assertions) literal-value assertions to the new values. Do NOT change the loop run / status exit MAPPINGS here (items 004/005) — only the const definition + member re-points so the package compiles.

items.title: Map loop run terminal outcome to the unified exit code
items.description: Replace the single terminal-exit ternary in packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts (~lines 979-983, currently `pausedReason === "needs_human" ? PAUSED_HUMAN : SUCCESS`) with the full LoopResult→exit-code mapping from 00-core-definitions.md §2a. Map over LoopResult (packages/loop/src/runner.ts ~:62-72): run failed/errored → ERROR(1); pausedReason==="needs_human" OR needsHumanCount>0 → NEEDS_HUMAN(3); limit-reached/usage-paused/sleeping terminal → LIMIT(4); blockedCount>0 → BLOCKED(5); otherwise (clean: completed/idle/cancelled-graceful) → SUCCESS(0). RUNNING(6) is NEVER a terminal code. If LoopResult has no explicit limit carrier, derive it as 03-exit-codes.md §3 describes (or document the known gap). Add a table-driven unit test over LoopResult shapes.
acceptanceCriteria: loop run returns the §2a code for each terminal outcome (error→1, needs_human→3, limit→4, blocked→5, clean→0)

items.title: Rewrite statusExitCode to the unified scheme (+ derived BLOCKED)
items.description: Rewrite `statusExitCode` in packages/cli/src/status-commands.ts (~lines 492-504) to the unified state→code mapping from 00-core-definitions.md §2b, over LoopStateEnum (packages/core/src/schemas.ts ~:228-239): RUNNING→RUNNING(6); PAUSED_HUMAN→NEEDS_HUMAN(3); LIMIT_REACHED/SLEEPING_LIMIT/WEEKLY_LIMIT→LIMIT(4); ERROR→ERROR(1); IDLE/COMPLETE/PAUSED/NOT_INSTALLED→SUCCESS(0). Additionally support derived BLOCKED(5): a clean terminal state (IDLE/COMPLETE/PAUSED) WITH genuine-blocked>0 → BLOCKED(5). `blocked` is NOT a LoopStateEnum value, so this requires widening the signature to `statusExitCode(state, derived)` and consulting the backlog summary's genuine-blocked count (see status-commands genuineBlocked). If the widening is deferred, document it as a known gap per 03-exit-codes.md §4. Tests: an it.each over the 10 LoopStateEnum values + a separate derived-BLOCKED case.

items.title: Add loop run --detached; remove loop start (fold into shared helper)
items.description: Implement the execution-grammar collapse from 02-execution-grammar.md §2. In packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts: add a `--detached`/`-d` branch to `handleLoopRun` (~:620) — when set, delegate to the EXISTING server path: `ensureServerRunning(ctx)` (~:258-286, unchanged) then POST /api/projects/:id/loop/start using the same request body builder loop-commands.ts uses today (~:334-357), then return immediately (printing the `rauf follow <path>` hint). Bare `loop run` keeps the existing in-process `LoopRunner.create().start()` path, unchanged. Remove `handleLoopStart` (~:290) as a dispatchable verb: drop the `loop start` subcommand from the registry in packages/cli/src/commands.ts, and fold handleLoopStart's body into a shared detached helper invoked by the --detached branch (no logic duplication). In packages/cli/src/parser.ts, add `-d` as the short alias for `--detached`. Do NOT change execution semantics (server still runs the loop in-process via LoopManager) and do NOT change the POST /loop/start route. Do NOT implement the removed-command remediation message here (item 009) beyond the verb no longer being dispatchable.
acceptanceCriteria: loop run --detached (and -d) delegates to ensureServerRunning + POST /loop/start and returns immediately (assert with the server mocked); does NOT create an in-process LoopRunner

items.title: Compose --detached --follow with view-only Ctrl-C lifecycle
items.description: Implement `loop run --detached --follow` per 02-execution-grammar.md §3. After the detached server POST returns (item 006), attach the canonical top-level `follow` view CLI-side. `--follow` is an observation concern handled entirely CLI-side AFTER the POST returns — it MUST NOT be added to the server request body (the body carries only loop options). Lifecycle: interrupting the attached view (Ctrl-C) detaches the VIEW ONLY — it must NOT issue POST /loop/stop and must NOT stop the loop; the loop keeps running server-side. Stopping a detached run requires an explicit `loop stop`. Add tests for both the no-follow-in-body invariant and the Ctrl-C-detaches-only behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: loop run --detached --follow attaches the top-level follow view after the POST returns
--follow is NOT included in the server request body
Ctrl-C on the attached view detaches the view only (no POST /loop/stop, loop keeps running)
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test passes

items.title: Apply the flag canon across the CLI read/run surface

items.title: Add targeted remediation errors for removed verbs/flags
items.description: Implement removed-command remediation per 00-core-definitions.md §5 and 02-execution-grammar.md §7. Invoking a removed verb/flag must exit USAGE(2) with a targeted message naming the replacement, executing NOTHING (this is an error message, NOT an alias — it must not run the replacement). Lookup table: `loop start` → "`loop start` was removed in v0.5.0 — use `loop run --detached` (`-d`)."; `--watch` (on any command) → "`--watch` was removed in v0.5.0 — use `--follow` (`-f`).". The interceptor must fire BEFORE the generic unknown-subcommand / unknown-flag error so the targeted message wins. Loci: the command dispatch in packages/cli/src/commands.ts (for `loop start`) and the flag-parsing path in packages/cli/src/parser.ts (for `--watch`). Add tests asserting the exact messages, the USAGE(2) exit, and that nothing is executed.
acceptanceCriteria: `rauf loop start ...` exits USAGE(2) with the message naming `loop run --detached`, and starts no loop (no server POST, no LoopRunner)
`--watch` on any command exits USAGE(2) with the message naming `--follow`, executing nothing
The remediation fires before the generic unknown-subcommand/unknown-flag error (assert the specific message)
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test passes
items.notes: Depends on 003 (USAGE) and 006 (loop start removed). Not an alias — executes nothing. 00 §5 + 02 §7 are authoritative.
